newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to investigate high petrol pump prices.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to investigate high petrol pump prices.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Friday it is to investigate why diesel and petrol prices in the Netherlands are so much higher than in neighbouring countries.

The move by the Ministry of Economic Affairs comes after research by accountants Coopers and Lybrand on the differences between the "bare" prices (price less excise, tax and other levies) of Euro 95 gasoline and diesel in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, France and Britain.
"The research showed that the distribution margins vary widely. For Euro 95, (the margin in) Netherlands is out of line," the Economics Ministry said in a statement.
The report showed that distribution margins had risen by 15 percent in the Netherlands in the past two years, while remaining static in Belgium, Germany and France and halving in Britain.
"Coopers and Lybrand found no objective explanation for the differences," the ministry statement said.

It added that Dutch drivers were paying far more than if the distribution margins of the other countries applied -- 80 million guilders more than with the Belgian margin and 1.3 billion guilders more than with the average British margin.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs, which will be conducting the investigations, will also address two other related matters -- why there are so few newcomers to the fuel market and whether oil companies allow service stations to set prices independently.
